Reason: Joint profit is maximized by setting the highest price customers will pay, since the unconstrained monopoly price exceeds the $2.89 ceiling and this supports high-price coordination in the long run.

Recommended price: 2.89

Q=a-bp => profit (p-1)(a-bp). optimum p=(a/b+1)/2 = (126.3/21.7 +1)/2=(5.82+1)/2=3.41, above max WTP 2.89. So unconstrained monopoly price > max; choose max WTP 2.89 to maximize combined profit if collusive. But competition? If one raises while other lower, loses quantity.
